s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling of the hard palate with slow and symmetrical growth
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically over 10-12 weeks
Firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
key_facts: 41-year-old man with no significant medical history
10-12 week history of painless swelling
Swelling located in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically
Denies dysphagia, odynophagia, or systemic symptoms
Family history is unremarkable
1.5 x 3.0 cm firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
No cervical lymphadenopathy detected
Routine serum chemistry within normal limits
Serologies for hepatitis A, B, and C were negative
Palatal bone appeared uninvolved during excision

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a painless, slow-growing swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Central Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of painless swelling in the jaw, including the hard palate

shortlist.label: Torus Palatinus
shortlist.why_kept: Benign bony growth that can cause a slow-growing, painless swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of salivary gland tumor, can present as a painless swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Peripheral Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause a painless, slow-growing swelling on the hard palate, although less common than central giant cell granuloma

raw.rationale: The swelling is described as a firm, elastic, non-ulcerated growth located on the hard palate, which is consistent with Torus Palatinus, a benign bony growth that typically occurs in the midline of the hard palate but can also occur bilaterally.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Lesion
rejected.why: Giant cell lesions are typically more aggressive and may cause systemic symptoms, which the patient denies

rejected.label: Central Giant Cell Granuloma
rejected.why: Central giant cell granuloma usually involves the jawbone and can cause pain or looseness of teeth, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic adenoma is a type of salivary gland tumor that is usually found in the parotid gland, not the hard palate

rejected.label: Peripheral Giant Cell Granuloma
rejected.why: Peripheral giant cell granuloma typically presents as a solitary, ulcerated lesion on the gingiva, which does not match the patient's symptoms
